decision_note: Primary Erysimum capitatum study combines observational and experimental work across four populations/years to evaluate pollinator and herbivore preferences, plant fitness and selection on floral traits; retain as a strong multi-agent context/selection source.
Short addendum on floral signals establishing ant pollination mutualism in Cytinus; ants are effective pollinators in the focal work and no measured plant antagonist/exploiter channel is established.
Sexually deceptive daisy study links pollinator phylogeography/mate preference to floral divergence but lacks a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.
Bat-flower network study concerns spatiotemporal overlap and morphology in pollination microstructure without a focal plant antagonist/exploiter channel.
Science commentary 'The Invisible Bouquet' is not an independent primary study or sufficiently focused SCH synthesis.

Sidalcea hendersonii gynodioecy programme includes Bombus pollination observations, sex-biased seed predation, viable seed production and survival; retain for pollinator/predator/fitness adjudication.
Phenylpropene-synthase molecular-evolution study characterizes enzyme lineages without ecological pollinator and antagonist receiver responses.
Nicotiana africana study measures alkaloids and herbivory without a focal pollinator service/response.
Highbush-blueberry pollination-ecology thesis focuses pollinator abundance/effectiveness and crop pollination without a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.
Acacia population-genetics/dispersal thesis does not center a floral trait/reward coordinate with pollinator and antagonist responses.
Focused review synthesizes how herbivory changes floral traits, pollinator visitation and fruit/seed production; retain as relevant synthesis/source-chasing material.
Honey-bee larval parasite on flowers reduces pollinator visitation, but the parasite acts on the pollinator rather than as a plant antagonist/exploiter channel.
Genomics review focuses plant-pollinator interactions without a focal plant antagonist/exploiter channel.

Primary macro-comparative study tests whether insect-herbivore richness predicts plant sexual/mating traits that control outcrossing and dependence on pollinators; retain for evolutionary mutualist-antagonist trait adjudication.
Repository/data identity of the Red Queen herbivore-pressure versus plant mating-strategy study; retain at TA stage and resolve report dependence with SCHPRISMA-000810 at full text.
American Journal of Botany commentary/review on comparative biochemistry is not a focused plant pollinator-antagonist floral-trait synthesis.
Mediterranean-perspective review concerns pollinator roles in floral evolution without a focal plant antagonist/exploiter channel.

Repository identity of Veratrum mast-flowering study measuring pollination success, floral-stem herbivory, seed predation and seed production across habitats/years; retain and resolve report dependence with SCHPRISMA-000818 at full text.

Published Veratrum study measures pollination success, floral-stem herbivory, seed predation and seed production across lowland/alpine populations and years. Pollination success is null with respect to floral density, making it a valid negative/one-sided multi-agent source.

Focused review of nectar-robbing sensory/cognitive ecology explicitly covers switching between legitimate and robbing behaviour and consequences for plant fitness, natural selection and floral evolution; retain as role-boundary synthesis.
Study of commercial honeybee effects on invertebrate flower-visitor communities lacks a focal plant floral trait/reward coordinate and plant reproductive endpoint.

Primary Breynia floral-scent study is embedded in an obligate pollination-seed-consumption mutualism with Epicephala; post-pollination scent change is discussed as limiting ovary overexploitation by seed-predator pollinators. Retain for coupled-role signal adjudication.
Sunbird visitation/pollen-transport network study concerns pollination only, without a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.
New Phytologist commentary 'The sweet stench of decay' comments on carrion-flower scent chemistry/pollination and is not an independent primary study or focused SCH synthesis.
Schiedea study links floral volatile timing to shared pollinator foraging activity without a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.
